🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A Utah teenager who vanished nearly 18 months ago has been found safe in Oregon, and federal authorities have charged a 39-year-old man in connection with her alleged captivity.

Kylie Arellano, now 17, vanished from Garden City, Utah, on May 29, 2025, when she was 15. She was rescued on November 1, 2026, from a home in Huntington, Oregon, by Oregon State Police and federal agents. She was taken for medical treatment.

Her path to freedom began in mid-October 2026, when she connected with another minor while playing the online game “Among Us.” A tip from that minor's parent led law enforcement to the home.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop in Ontario, Oregon. He has been charged in a federal complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah with transporting a minor across state lines with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. A complaint is only an allegation, and Harmel is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

According to the criminal complaint, Harmel allegedly groomed Arellano on gaming platforms before moving their contact to other social media apps, and allegedly drove from Oregon to Perry, Utah, to pick her up on or about May 29, 2025. The complaint alleges he became “very violent and aggressive, often hitting” her, and forced her to remove her braces with pliers so that she could not be identified. A search of his residence allegedly uncovered knives, BB guns and sexual lubricant.

Arellano's mother, Stephanie Kaye, publicly identified her daughter and wrote, “THANK YOU GOD MY BABY IS SAFE!!” U.S. Attorney for the District of Utah Melissa Holyoak said the priority in the case was the “safe return of the minor victim.” FBI Director Kash Patel said local police in Oregon “brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety.”

Sources: New York Post; People; Fox News Digital; NBC News; KSL News.

title: Beyond the 956: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano found safe in Oregon after 17 months
